module_title: Specific Heat, Latent Heat, and Thermal Expansion
introduction: This level explains how different materials react to heat. Some materials heat up instantly, while others (like water) take a lot of energy to change temperature. It also covers what happens when matter changes its state.

core_concepts.title: Specific Heat Capacity (c)
core_concepts.description:
The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by $1^\circ\text{C}$ (or $1\text{K}$). 
Water has an extremely HIGH specific heat capacity ($4200 \text{ J/kg}^\circ\text{C}$). This is why water is used as a coolant in car radiators and why coastal areas have moderate climates.

core_concepts.title: Latent Heat (Hidden Heat)
core_concepts.description:
The heat required to change the STATE of a substance without changing its temperature. 
1. Latent Heat of Fusion: Solid to Liquid (Melting ice at $0^\circ\text{C}$). 
2. Latent Heat of Vaporization: Liquid to Gas (Boiling water at $100^\circ\text{C}$).

core_concepts.title: Anomalous Expansion of Water
core_concepts.description:
Most liquids expand when heated and contract when cooled. Water behaves differently. As water cools from $4^\circ\text{C}$ to $0^\circ\text{C}$, it EXPANDS instead of contracting. 
Conclusion: Water has its MAXIMUM density and MINIMUM volume exactly at $4^\circ\text{C}$.

important_entities.name: Steam vs. Boiling Water
important_entities.significance: Both boiling water and steam can be at $100^\circ\text{C}$. However, steam contains massive amounts of extra hidden energy called 'Latent Heat of Vaporization' ($22.6 \times 10^5 \text{ J/kg}$), making steam burns much more severe.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: 'What happens to the temperature of water while it is boiling?' Students often say it increases. FALSE. During a phase change (melting or boiling), the temperature remains strictly CONSTANT until the entire substance has changed state.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Water is heaviest (densest) at $4^\circ\text{C}$. This is why ice floats, and aquatic life survives in frozen lakes (the bottom layer of water remains at $4^\circ\text{C}$ and doesn't freeze).

exam_strategy_tips: State PCS Exams frequently ask: 'Why do water pipes burst in winter?' Answer: Anomalous expansion of water (water expands as it freezes into ice, putting immense pressure on the pipes).
